headline: Every carton checked, not a sample.
label: #FFFFFF
heroLede: Vitasoy's Wodonga plant has been making plant milk since 2002, and its output has grown about sevenfold since then, to around 70 million litres a year. The range now covers soy, oat, almond, coconut and rice milks. With that many varieties going into similar 1 litre cartons, the label is what tells one from the next, and allergens like soy and almond make a mix-up serious. This is what a camera check could look like on a plant milk carton line. Scroll through, then adjust the estimate at the end to your own numbers.
lidLede: The camera checks every carton has its cap on, straight and fully closed, and the carton top is sealed. A loose cap or a weak top seal means a leak in transit and a claim from the retailer.
labelLede: Oat and almond cartons look much the same at line speed. The camera checks every carton carries the right print for the milk inside, so nobody with an almond allergy gets almond in an oat carton.
codeLede: The best-before and batch code has to be right and readable on every carton. The system reads the printed code and compares it with the variety and date set at changeover.
objectLede: Cap offcuts, straw wrappers and loose parts can end up on the conveyor. The camera over the belt spots anything that should not be there before it reaches a tray.

vocab.alert: Four crooked caps in fifteen minutes on Line 1. Check the capper.

extra: 38% of Australian food recalls in 2025 were for undeclared allergens, with packaging errors among the main causes. FSANZ
With around 70 million litres a year, even one wrong carton in ten thousand is thousands of cartons. That is our example figure, not yours.
